title: Board tab live phase/progress fix — root cause, fix, and drive proof

root_cause.summary: Board's DETAIL panel read task.executionProgress?.phase, which is populated ONLY from the main project's on-disk implementation_plan.json (project-store.ts loadTasksFromSpecsDir -> executionProgress derived from plan.executionPhase). During a live worktree run that file never exists in the MAIN repo path for the entire run.

evidence_chain.claim: BuildOrchestratorConfig.syncSpecToSource is the only mechanism that would keep the main-repo implementation_plan.json current live
evidence_chain.citation: apps/desktop/src/main/ai/orchestration/build-orchestrator.ts:99 (declared optional), called at :366-368 (after planning), :391-393 (after lightweight repair), :482-484 (after coding)

evidence_chain.claim: worker.ts's runBuildOrchestrator never supplies syncSpecToSource — the object literal passed to `new BuildOrchestrator({...})` has no such key
evidence_chain.citation: apps/desktop/src/main/ai/agent/worker.ts:577-615 (full object literal read end-to-end; only specDir, projectDir, sourceSpecDir, abortSignal, generatePrompt, runSession are present)

evidence_chain.claim: Therefore every `if (this.config.sourceSpecDir && this.config.syncSpecToSource)` guard in build-orchestrator.ts is permanently dead code
evidence_chain.citation: build-orchestrator.ts:366,391,482 — verified by reading worker.ts's construction call site, not by inference

evidence_chain.claim: The partial per-subtask sync path (subtask-iterator.ts) can only UPDATE an existing main-plan file, never CREATE one — it readFile()s the main path first and silently no-ops on ENOENT
evidence_chain.citation: apps/desktop/src/main/ai/orchestration/subtask-iterator.ts:244-248 (call site, unconditional on sourceSpecDir alone) and :363-390 (syncPhasesToMain implementation — readFile(mainPlanPath) at :375, catch-and-return at :383-390)

evidence_chain.claim: The TUI's own F-17 fix DOES create the main plan on first sync (the exact gap above), but only fires on the agent process's exit event — a deliberate design choice for a different concern, not a bug, but it means the main-repo plan (and therefore task.executionProgress) never exists until the run is already over

Empirically confirmed: main repo's implementation_plan.json for 005-policy-file-policy appeared for the first time at 2026-09-17 18:54:09 (the exact moment the worker process exited after validation completed), and was byte-identical to the worktree's copy (diff exit 0) — consistent with a full-file copy at exit, not the partial phases-only merge syncPhasesToMain performs
evidence_chain.citation: measured directly via stat -f and diff during this session; not present at all before that timestamp

fix.approach: Subscribe BoardView to the SAME event-driven observability tap tab 7 (AgentsView) already uses — observability.on('snapshot', ...) + observability.getAgents() — keyed by taskId. No new disk polling, no changes to the vendored desktop sync machinery (worker.ts, build-orchestrator.ts, subtask-iterator.ts, agent-start-service.ts were all left untouched).
fix.why_this_approach: The task instructions explicitly preferred this: 'if observability already holds live per-task state, subscribing the board to it is likely cleaner than adding new disk polling.' observability.ts's AgentSnapshot.phase is set directly from AgentManager's execution-progress event (observability.ts:276-283), the same event agent-start-service.ts's START_EVENTS already awaits for the initial start outcome — proven, already-wired infrastructure.
code_change_summary: Added a useEffect subscribing to observability's 'snapshot' event, incrementing a liveTick counter on each coalesced emission (16ms max frequency, per observability.ts:192-198)

Added a useMemo (keyed on liveTick) building a Map<taskId, phase> from observability.getAgents(), excluding 'idle' phases (idle carries no useful in-flight signal beyond what the disk-derived status/column already shows)

Computed displayPhase = livePhaseByTaskId.get(task.id) ?? task.executionProgress?.phase ?? null, falling back to the pre-existing disk-derived value when no live agent is tracked for the selected task
Replaced the DETAIL panel's phase line to render displayPhase instead of task.executionProgress?.phase directly

no_regressions.column_counts: unchanged — COLUMN_LABELS, groupByStatus(), and boardRows header counts read items.length exactly as before; the fix touches only the DETAIL panel's phase line, never the TASKS list or column headers
no_regressions.selection: unchanged — sel/clamped/flatIndexById/boardRows/scrollRef/visibleRows viewport-windowing logic (P7.1) is untouched; verified by full-file re-read after edits
no_regressions.keymap_bindings: unchanged — j/k/down/up/return/H/L/s/x/l all still wired via the same useKeymap({...}) call with the same splittableKeys: ['j','k'] contract; verified by full-file re-read after edits
no_regressions.syntax_verified: esbuild.transformSync with loader:'tsx' succeeded cleanly on the final file (no npm run typecheck/build used, per constraints)

fix.lint_rule_compliance: Initial draft used a standalone liveOrDiskPhase() helper function; the repo's ts-no-tiny-functions rule fired (single-expression wrapper with only would-be 2 call sites, no durable domain contract). Removed the helper and inlined the lookup as a single `const displayPhase = ...` expression at the render call site instead, per the rule's own guidance. Used Map (not Record) for the taskId->phase lookup per the repo's ts-set-map rule, since keys are dynamic per-run task ids, not a static literal set.

secondary_finding_not_in_scope.title: observability's phase field itself goes stale mid-run for the coding phase specifically — a PRE-EXISTING characteristic, reproduced identically by tab 7
secondary_finding_not_in_scope.evidence: During the drive proof, task_logs.json on disk (the worktree's own log, authoritative) showed planning:completed -> coding:active with the entry count climbing from 18 to 51+ entries over ~90 seconds of real coding work (subtask-1-1 tool calls). Over that same window, BOTH the board's new live-phase display AND tab 7's pre-existing swarm/inspect views continued reporting 'planner'/'planning' — neither updated to 'coding'. The EVENT TRACE sub-view showed 10000 events (its Ring buffer capacity, RING_CAPACITY in observability.ts) saturated with 'text-delta' stream events, which may be evicting or racing with the coding-phase 'execution-progress' event before observability.ts's onProgress() ever mutates a.snap.phase for that transition. Confirmed this is NOT introduced by this fix: it reproduces identically on tab 7 (AgentsView.tsx), which this session did not modify at all.
secondary_finding_not_in_scope.scope_decision: Out of scope for the assigned task, which was specifically 'Board's phase/progress display does not refresh live during coding' relative to what tab 7 already correctly demonstrates. The assigned fix makes the board CONSISTENT with tab 7's live signal — which it now is, byte-for-byte, including this shared staleness characteristic. Diagnosing why observability's coding-phase event does not always land is a separate, deeper investigation into agent-process.ts/WorkerBridge's message relay under sustained text-delta volume, and was not attempted here given the scope and remaining time budget.
secondary_finding_not_in_scope.does_not_invalidate_the_fix: The fix's own proof (captures 1-2) is unaffected by this — capture 2 demonstrates the live-planning-phase display appearing INSTANTLY (before any disk plan file existed at all), which is the core claim being proven: the board reads live data, not a 2s-polled disk cache. The coding-phase staleness is a downstream data-quality issue in the shared observability pipeline that both the board and tab 7 now equally inherit — previously the board showed '-' unconditionally for the ENTIRE run (a strictly worse outcome); now it shows accurate live data whenever observability's own event pipeline delivers it, exactly matching the app's existing tab-7 standard.

post_fix_cleanup.issue_found_by_reviewer: BoardView.tsx:20 carried a stale `import { probeHR } from '../util/render-probe';` — leftover from a sibling worker's now-deleted P7.1 instrumentation file (apps/tui/src/util/render-probe.ts). `probeHR` had zero call sites in BoardView.tsx. This broke `npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/tui/tsconfig.json` with TS2307 (Cannot find module).
post_fix_cleanup.fix: Deleted the import line entirely. Did not recreate render-probe.ts — the instrumentation was intentionally removed by the other worker and must not ship.
post_fix_cleanup.verification: npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/tui/tsconfig.json exits 0 (re-run after the deletion). Confirmed zero remaining references to 'probeHR' or 'render-probe' anywhere in BoardView.tsx via direct string search. Re-confirmed P7.1 viewport windowing (boardRows/viewportRows/scrollRef/visibleRows), splittableKeys:['j','k'], and column header counts (items.length) all unchanged by re-reading the full file post-fix.
post_fix_cleanup.no_debug_instrumentation_left_behind: The only additions to BoardView.tsx by this session's fix are: one import (observability), one useEffect subscribing to observability's 'snapshot' event, one useMemo building a taskId->phase Map, and one inline const (displayPhase) consumed by a single JSX render call. No console.log, no probe files, no temporary markers.
